prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Labour’s 2024 offer is a mission-driven plan to stop 14 years of Conservative chaos, turn the page on short-termism and division, and rebuild a Britain that serves working people. It restores security—in the economy, at the border, on our streets, in energy, and in public services—through partnership with business, trade unions and communities, anchored in fiscal responsibility.

Foundations: security, borders, stability
- National security: Unshakeable NATO commitment and the UK’s nuclear deterrent; Strategic Defence Review in year one; path to 2.5% of GDP on defence; tougher counter-espionage and counter-extremism; Martyn’s Law for public venues.
- Secure borders: New Border Security Command using counter‑terror style powers; scrap Rwanda scheme and clear the asylum backlog with more caseworkers and returns; new EU security agreement and joint policing; fast-track removal for those with no right to stay.
- Economic stability: Strict fiscal rules; OBR oversight of all fiscal events; keep NI, Income Tax rates and VAT unchanged; modernise HMRC; abolish non‑dom status; close avoidance loopholes; tackle cost-of-living drivers (energy, food, housing, childcare).

Five national missions
1) Kickstart economic growth
- Pro‑business, pro‑worker “securonomics” and a statutory Industrial Strategy Council.
- National Wealth Fund (£7.3bn) to crowd in private investment in ports, gigafactories, steel, CCS and green hydrogen.
- Planning reform and devolution to build 1.5m homes, new towns, brownfield-first with targeted “grey belt” release; permanent mortgage guarantee; biggest boost to social/affordable housing in a generation.
- Replace business rates in England; cap corporation tax at 25% for the Parliament; permanent full expensing; 10‑year infrastructure strategy; rail brought into public ownership as contracts expire; powers for mayors to integrate transport; national 5G/gigabit by 2030.
- New Deal for Working People: day‑one rights, ban exploitative zero-hours and fire‑and‑rehire, single enforcement body; minimum wage that reflects the cost of living.

2) Make Britain a clean energy superpower
- Clean power by 2030: double onshore wind, triple solar, quadruple offshore wind; new nuclear (Sizewell C, SMRs); CCS, hydrogen and storage; no new North Sea exploration licences (manage existing fields responsibly); no fracking.
- Great British Energy (£8.3bn), publicly owned, headquartered in Scotland; Local Power Plan; grid overhaul; British Jobs Bonus to rebuild supply chains.
- Warm Homes Plan: upgrade 5m homes; tough water regulation, automatic fines for polluters; support for farmers; stronger animal welfare.

3) Take back our streets
- Neighbourhood Policing Guarantee with thousands more officers/PCSOs; Respect Orders to tackle antisocial behaviour; specific offence for assaults on shopworkers.
- Knife crime plan: mandatory interventions, curfews/tagging, ban zombie/ninja blades; Young Futures hubs in every community; new child criminal exploitation offence.
- Halve serious violence; specialist rape units in every force; fast‑track rape courts; tougher vetting and misconduct rules; major fraud strategy.

4) Break down barriers to opportunity
- 3,000 new school‑based nurseries; free breakfast clubs in every primary; recruit 6,500 teachers in key subjects; modern curriculum and assessment; mental health support in every school.
- Skills England; devolved adult skills; turn FE colleges into Technical Excellence Colleges; reform Apprenticeship Levy into a flexible Growth & Skills Levy.
- Family security: child poverty strategy; abolish Section 21 evictions; leasehold and ground rent reform; homelessness strategy.
- Equality: new Race Equality Act; disability and ethnicity pay-gap reporting; trans‑inclusive ban on conversion practices; modernise gender recognition while upholding Equality Act single‑sex exceptions.

5) Build an NHS fit for the future
- Cut waiting times with 40,000 extra weekly appointments; pooled waiting lists; use spare independent capacity; workforce plan.
- Double CT/MRI scanners; deliver New Hospitals Programme; modernised NHS app; family doctor model; stronger primary care with pharmacist prescribing.
- Dentistry Rescue Plan (700,000 urgent appointments); National Care Service with fair pay agreement; 8,500 additional mental health staff; bold public health action (smoking, vapes to children, junk food ads).

Clean up politics, reconnect Britain
- Ethics and Integrity Commission; modernise Commons; immediate Lords reforms (end hereditary peers, retirement age), toward a more representative second chamber; votes at 16; stronger devolution and intergovernmental respect.
- Rebuild global leadership: firm on Ukraine, AUKUS, and China strategy; make Brexit work (practical EU deals on trade, security, qualifications, touring); focused trade strategy; restore development leadership (road to 0.7%) and lead a global Clean Power Alliance.

First steps for change
- Economic stability; 40,000 extra NHS appointments a week; Border Security Command; Great British Energy; neighbourhood policing crackdown; 6,500 new teachers—paid for by closing tax loopholes and ending waste.
